brief: US Treasuries sold off Wednesday: higher oil prices and strong economic data lifted Fed tightening expectations, and a weak USD 70bn five-year auction added pressure, pushing the 10-year yield up nearly 15 basis points to above 5.1%, a first since 2007, while the S&P 500 fell 0.8%. The S&P Global flash PMI rose to 58.4, a fourth straight month of acceleration and the strongest since July 2021, though input costs rose fastest in nearly four years. Fed funds futures now price a 70% chance of an October hike, up from near 50% a week earlier. UBS argues tightening will be less aggressive than priced: its base case is a December hike then a hold through 2027, with disinflation ahead and a 0.2 percentage point downward core PCE revision expected, keeping it constructive on equities and fixed income. Separately, the Franco-German bond spread hit its widest since 2012 on French fiscal and election concerns, gold slid on Fed hawkishness though UBS holds a USD 5,400/oz 2027 target, and UBS called a rumored US diesel export ban counterproductive.
